newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher, but lag Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher, but lag Dow rally.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended higher on Thursday, but Canada's leading stock market failed to match the exuberance of its bigger U.S. counterpart.
The TSE 300 Composite Index climbed 29.38 points to close at 5959.36 in brisk turnover of 103.63 million shares worth C$1.58 billion ($1.16 billion).
By comparison, the Dow Jones Industrial Average soared more than 76 points to a record close of 6625.67 on favorable economic data.
Ron Meisels, portfolio consultant and president of P and C Holdings Ltd., said the TSE struggled to push through 5960, but "eventually Toronto will go the way of New York."
Meisels said large cap stocks have attracted most of the buying in New York. But investors are expected to jump into small cap issues and that will benefit Canadian stocks.
"Even though we have some billion dollar companies, Canada is thought of as a small cap country. When small caps in New York start to move, it's likely Canada will move," he said.
In today's action, precious metals jumped 261 points to lead 13 of Toronto's 14 sub-groups aloft.
Golds were followed by modest gains in energy, transportation, pipelines and base metals. The lone weak sector was financial services.
* Gulf Canada Resources Ltd. led heavy traders, closing up 0.25 at 10.95 on 3.5 million shares following a recent share issue. The stock earlier hit a 52-week high of 11.25.
* Among gold stocks, Golden Rule Resources Ltd. jumped 1.20 to 7.85 on 1.5 million shares after reaching a 52-week peak of 7.95.
Bema Gold Corp. rose 0.90 to 8.10 on 2.1 million shares.
Despite a rebound in gold prices on Thursday, analysts predicted the recent weak trend to continue and further batter Canadian gold stocks.
* Manitoba Telecom Ltd. remained active in its first week as a public firm, ending flat at 8.20 on 2.5 million shares.
